protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED file-08 content change under D-001 MF-6, bound by D-086 rider RB-GHN-V3-A1
summary: This is the write the rider constrained, and it stays inside every constraint. All sixteen prefixes reproduce v3's harnessId strings character for character and the named set is order-equal to v3's recordable sixteen, with G03, G04, G13 and G17 each given a prefix that denies naming rather than asserting it. The quoted current condition-4 cell is verbatim and unique in file 08. The claim I expected to fail is clause 5's — that the 'What that means' paragraph needs no edit — and it holds: I read the paragraph in full and it makes no harness claim at all, and a sweep of the whole register found exactly one statement anywhere that goes stale at zero-to-sixteen, which is the cell being rewritten. The new cell carries forward '19 OPEN, 3 HARD-BLOCKED' and 'every assurance stage is below QUALIFIED', and I re-derived both from the gate table rather than assuming they survived. Two non-blocking notes.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, 'Reversibility': 'C-D088 plus restore of the prior 20 harness-cell prefixes (16 named + G03/G04/G13/G17)'
notesNonBlocking.observation: There are no prior prefixes. This entry inserts twenty prefixes into cells that currently have none, so the reversal is removal of what D-088 added, not restoration of something that was displaced. The count and the enumeration are right — sixteen named plus G03, G04, G13 and G17 is exactly the twenty cells the entry touches, and I confirmed the prefix table has exactly twenty rows — and the intent is recoverable from the parallel clause about 'the prior condition-4 Measured now cell', where 'prior' does correctly denote displaced content. Recorded because the reversibility clause is the instruction an overturn executes, and a reader following it literally would look for prior prefixes and find none. 'Removal of the 20 harness-cell prefixes this entry inserts' would say it exactly.

All sixteen named prefixes attribute to D-086 alone — none of the sixteen cites D-088 — while the condition-4 replacement cell the same entry writes cites '(D-086 / D-088)'. The attribution is not wrong: D-086 is where the identifiers come from, and the write act is traceable through the C-D088 commit and the COORD entry. But the entry models the fuller form in its own summary cell, and a later reader inspecting a harness cell in isolation has no pointer to the decision that put the text there. Naming both, as the condition-4 cell does, would make the twenty cells self-describing on the same terms.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: bf422872713bf6337b0e12a1ecefacde504ac8255276c393422d911d32e81d62, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at d313a460… across start and end.

The attack 'prefixes disagree with v3 harness IDs' fails on an exact-string test rather than a reading. I parsed all twenty prefix rows, matched each named prefix against the pattern 'named: <id> (D-086; not authored; not QUALIFIED).', and compared the extracted identifier to that gate's harnessId in v3. Sixteen of sixteen match character for character, with zero mismatches and zero malformed rows.

The set is right as well as the strings. The sixteen gates given named prefixes are order-equal to v3's recordable sixteen, which I derived independently as the gates whose sliceStanding starts with REQUIRED and whose namingStanding is NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED. None of G03, G04, G06, G11, G13 or G17 appears among them.

The attack 'writes G03/G04 as named' fails and does so affirmatively rather than by omission. Both receive 'reserved, not named (D-006 machine pins owed; D-086).' — a prefix that records the reservation and the reason it stands. Clause 2 states they 'remain required and unnamed', and the new condition-4 cell repeats it. This satisfies the rider's 'Do not write G03/G04 as named until the D-006-conforming naming act lands.'

The attack 'writes G17 as required-now' fails: G17 receives 'dropped / inapplicable (D-077 SARIF drop; D-086). not required-now.', which satisfies the rider's second prohibition explicitly. G13 receives a reservation prefix naming DR-118 and zero C4 progress, consistent with its exclusion from the eighteen.

The attack 'presents 16 of 16' fails. The new cell reads '16 of 18 required gates name a recorded identifier', the rejected alternative 'Present 16 of 16. Rejected: GHN-V2-B1 / RB-GHN-V3-A1' is present, and the readiness effect says '16 of 18 required'. Eighteen is the denominator throughout, which is what the rider's 'Do not present 16 as the required-gate denominator' requires.

The attack 'quoted current condition-4 cell is not verbatim' fails. The quoted Current string appears in file 08 exactly once and matches byte for byte, so the replacement targets a real and unambiguous cell.

Clause 5's claim about the 'What that means' paragraph is the one I most expected to fail, because a summary paragraph going stale behind a changed measurement is a defect I have missed in this corpus before. It holds. I read the paragraph in full: it contains no occurrence of 'harness', 'named', 'name', 'gate' or 'QUALIFIED', its only condition-4 statement is 'condition 4 is PARTLY MET', which survives the change, and the phrase clause 5 names does not appear in it. Leaving it unchanged is correct.

I did not stop at the paragraph the entry named. I swept the whole register for any other statement whose truth depends on the zero-named value — 'no gate names', '0 named', 'zero named', 'no concrete harness', 'no harness', 'concrete harness artifact', 'names a concrete', 'harness artifact' — and every non-gate-row occurrence of 'harness'. Exactly one statement in file 08 asserts that no gate names a harness, and it is the cell being rewritten. Line 378 and the condition-4 Required column state the requirement rather than a measurement and correctly stay unchanged.

The notes clause 6 protects are real and unaffected. D-070, D-081 and D-084 each did edit file 08 — I confirmed by commit stat rather than by searching for their IDs, which do not appear as literals — and their content is condition-1 rows, the disposition counts and the snapshot regeneration guidance. None makes a harness-naming claim, so none goes stale here.

The new cell re-asserts two carried-over claims, and rewriting a cell makes the entry responsible for all of it, so I re-derived both from the gate table instead of assuming they survived. Status lead labels tally to exactly 19 OPEN and 3 HARD-BLOCKED across the 22 rows, and no row's assurance stage asserts QUALIFIED — the values are SPECIFIED, 'PROPOSED; not QUALIFIED', 'BLOCKED by DR-002–008' and similar. Both claims are true after the write.

The new cell's wording does not overclaim against v3's own definition. v3's whatNamingIs is 'An identifier string per gate' and a future artifact path, and whatNamingIsNot includes 'Not a claim that any named path exists on disk. artifactExists is false for every row.' The cell says the gates 'name a recorded identifier' and each prefix says 'not authored; not QUALIFIED', which matches that definition rather than exceeding it.

The attack 'condition 4 claimed MET' fails on four surfaces: the header refusal, 'Standing stays PARTLY MET' under the replacement, the readiness effect's 'Condition 4 stays PARTLY MET', and the rejected alternative 'Mark condition 4 MET. Rejected: 16 of 18 is not all required gates named; MET is not QUALIFIED.'

The attack 'silent QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED / SATISFIED' fails on a line-by-line audit: every occurrence outside the prefix tables is a refusal or an unchanged standing, and inside the prefix tables 'not QUALIFIED' appears as a denial in all sixteen named prefixes.
The attack 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fails: both occurrences are refusals and the rejected alternative survives; condition 5 remains NOT MET and last in the readiness effect.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on every row. COORD 6dd90409…, file 08 ff2ebadd…, freeze e809d439… and v3 b5236612… all match live bytes. Both commits resolve at full hash: 14865abc… to 'D-086: record gate-harness-naming.v3 as C4 candidate' and 953b2311… to D-087. D-086 is present in COORD, so 'D-086 is ADOPTED' is true and this write is properly downstream of it; D-088 is absent, so adoption creates no collision.

The write is mechanically safe for the register's format: none of the twenty prefixes contains a pipe or backtick, so no inserted string can break the table row it enters. The prefix table has exactly twenty rows, matching the twenty cells the reversibility clause enumerates.
The snapshot heading date is already 2026-08-14, so clause 5's instruction not to change it leaves no stale date behind.
file 08 and COORD are unmodified in my working tree. I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of subject and prompt three times at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions; regex parse of all twenty prefix rows followed by pattern-match extraction of each harness identifier and character-for-character comparison against v3's harnessId field, plus set- and order-equality of the named gates against the recordable sixteen derived independently from v3's sliceStanding and namingStanding fields; exact-substring and occurrence-count test of the quoted Current condition-4 cell against file 08; full read of the 'What that means' paragraph with probe counts for harness, named, name, gate and QUALIFIED; register-wide sweep for eight distinct phrasings of the no-named-harness claim plus every non-gate-row occurrence of 'harness'; commit-stat inspection of D-070, D-081 and D-084 to locate their file-08 notes, which carry no literal decision IDs; column-header-based parse of the 22-row gate table to tally Status lead labels and enumerate assurance-stage values; character scan of all twenty prefixes for pipes and backticks that would break table rows; digest verification of all four pinned files and git log at full hash for both pinned commits; presence checks for D-086 and D-088 in COORD

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. A file-08 write is where an accepted naming quietly becomes an overclaim, so I tested the two places that would show it. The first is the strings: all sixteen reproduce v3 exactly, and the four gates that must not be named receive prefixes that say so rather than being silently omitted, which is the stronger construction because a missing cell reads as an oversight while a reservation reads as a decision. The second is staleness, and here the entry does something I have seen omitted before — it names the paragraph most likely to rot and states the test for it. I checked that claim and then went past it, sweeping the register for any other sentence that depends on there being no named harness; there is exactly one and it is the cell being replaced. The rewritten cell also re-asserts two inherited counts, which I re-derived from the gate table rather than letting them ride. Both notes are wording, not substance.
